transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Rajiv Malhotra (CTO - Nebularx), Elena Park (Platform Eng), Marcus Lee (Head of MLOps), Tanya Brooks (Security)

Auto summary (may be rough): Customer is evaluating reserved capacity for productionizing their genAI inference (drug-sim assistant). Primary asks: predictable 99th latency under 250ms for small chat workloads, strict tenant isolation, burst up to ~3x traffic for uncertain marketing spikes, and an eventual private/on-prem option to satisfy data residency.

[00:00] Liam: hi all thanks for joining, quick agenda - understand your stack, peaks, latency targets, security gates and then outline Redwood reserved options.
[00:18] Rajiv: thanks liam yeah we - i'm rajiv - and real quick we have a mixed workload. Some short chat prompts (30-120 tokens) and heavy batch rerank jobs. Latency for chat is critical.
[00:32] Elena: and we also have nightly bulk embedding runs but those can be on-hosted cheaper infra. Main focus is the live inference.
[00:45] Sofia: cool, can you quantify peak qps and expected p95 / p99? often that drives the prewarm sizing.
[00:52] Marcus: baseline is about 150 rps during office hours, peaks up to 420 rps on product launches; so planning for a 3x burst buffer seems reasonable. p95 is ~120ms today on their small model, p99 occasionally jets to 380ms which is bad for UX.
[01:12] Rajiv: and we have multi-tenant model - internal and customer tenants - need strong isolation, ideally dedicated GPU pools per tenant class. We looked at some of the other cloud vendors but isolation was fuzzy or costs exploded.
[01:33] Liam: ok makes sense; with Redwood Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools and apply tenant fencing - we support node-level tenancy and warm pools for burst. question: are you able to accept model quantization? that changes throughput a lot.
[01:49] Elena: we want to keep output fidelity - for drug-interaction scoring we cannot lose more than a tiny amount. Quantization is interesting but we'd want a perf/quality check.
[02:03] Sofia: totally, our Optimize team can recommend quant profiles per model and run evals to show delta. typically int8 gives big cost wins but we'll validate.
[02:19] Marcus: about prewarm / burst - curious how quick a warm pool can scale to 3x. if launch traffic comes in we need sub-60s scale up ideally.
[02:30] Liam: warm pools are pre-warmed containers/nodes; we can pre-provision a hotpool that accepts traffic immediately. For 3x you'd either keep a warm pool sized for the burst or use cold-to-hot scaling with prewarm windows; there is a cost tradeoff. we can present a couple of models in pricing.
[02:52] Rajiv: what about VPC/private? we have a roadmap to keep PHI inside our VPC later in the year. on-prem is also on the table for certain customers.
[03:02] Sofia: Redwood Private supports a customer-controlled VPC handshake and on-prem packages. Audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and you can run the control plane in a private subnet. sometimes people do a hybrid: hosted for low-sensitivity traffic and private for regulated tenants.
[03:17] Tanya: from security — do you support HSM/KMS and bring-your-own-key? also need proof of SOC2 and retention controls for logs.
[03:25] Liam: yes BYOK with KMS is supported for Private, and we have SOC2 Type II; i will attach our security pack. audit logs can be retained per customer policy.
[03:35] Marcus: ok costs — how do you price reserved nodes vs burst? give examples. we want a committed monthly and a burst buffer charged on usage.
[03:44] Liam: typical model - base reserved pool pricing (monthly commit) gives you predictable unit costs; burst is charged on top at a higher rate or via burst credits. we'll send examples: say 8-A100 equivalent reserved pool for Xk tokens/month vs on-demand during bursts.
[04:02] Elena: we need more concrete numbers to present to finance — and examples of how latency SLOs are guaranteed (SLA) or how fallbacks work when capacity exhausted.
[04:12] Sofia: fallbacks - we support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or region, with routing policies you can configure per route. we also expose traces to see retry behavior.
[04:26] Rajiv: on the topic of routing - can requests be routed by tenant? we want internal traffic on lower-cost path and paying customers on dedicated path.
[04:36] Liam: yes per-tenant routing is supported; you can pin model versions and policies. tenant routing + RBAC will let you ensure customer tenants hit dedicated nodes.
[04:49] Marcus: can we run a short benchmark? we'd like Redwood to run our sample workload against a reserved pool and show 95/99 latency numbers.
[04:56] Liam: absolutely, Sofia will share the perf harness and runbook. ideally you share a 7-day traffic histogram and we'll pick a 48-hour window for the smoke benchmark.
[05:08] Sofia: i'll upload the harness to a shared repo - it's fairly lightweight. pls note sometimes the transcriptions call it a per-f-harness — ignore that.
[05:18] Rajiv: what's the typical time to spin an on-prem pilot? we might need an air-gapped option for a partner.
[05:26] Sofia: for on-prem it usually take 4-8 weeks to provision and get the control plane in your subnet, shorter if network and procurement are ready. we'll scope it as a separate SOW.
[05:37] Tanya: about encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS between customer sidecar and the runtime?
[05:43] Liam: yes mTLS can be configured, plus you can use private link / VPC peering for network isolation.
[05:49] Elena: any limits on model size or kv cache persistence? we have long context state for few use cases.
[05:57] Sofia: runtime supports large KV caches; we can tune memory vs disk-backed cache and discuss snapshotting. model size supported depends on node class; we can run feasibility quickly.
[06:08] Marcus: one more - can we get logging to our SIEM? we need structured logs pushed to customer S3 or Splunk.
[06:15] Liam: yes we support log shipping, event streams and webhook hooks; we'll include log retention options in the pack.
[06:25] (brief crosstalk)
[06:30] Rajiv: ok recap - we want committed capacity for baseline, prewarm strategy for 3x bursts, tenant fencing per customer class, and an option for Private/on-prem later. next steps: pricing + perf harness + traffic hist.
[06:45] Liam: perfect. i'll send a pricing worksheet and SLA examples. sofia will send the benchmark harness and runbook. rajiv/tanya will share security scopes and traffic hist. we'll target a follow up workshop week of 2026-08-10 to review benchmark results and on-prem scoping.
[07:02] Sofia: quick note - sometimes the auto transcription shows KV cash or V P C spelled out weird.
[07:10] Elena: thanks all.
[07:12] Liam: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
Links referenced: Pricing worksheet (will be shared), Redwood security pack (SOC2), perf harness repo (link to be shared).

Transcript notes: The recording contains filler words and occasional transcription errors (e.g., KV cash for KV cache, V-P-C spelled out). Speaker labels sometimes generic.
